b1: How to Get to Colmar by Train
b2: By WoW Train · Updated June 2026 · 3 min read
b3: Half-timbered houses in candy colours, flower-lined canals, cobbled lanes — Colmar is the "Little Venice" of Alsace, and one of the prettiest towns in France. Best of all: you can be there from Paris in barely more than two hours.
b5: Direct high-speed trains run from Paris (Gare de l'Est) to Colmar several times a day, taking around 2h20 on the fastest services. If you're coming from elsewhere — Strasbourg, Basel or further afield — Colmar sits right on the main Alsace line, so connections are easy and frequent.
b7: 1. Board a direct TGV from Paris Gare de l'Est to Colmar (or connect via Strasbourg).
b8: 2. Arrive at Colmar station, right in the city.
b9: 3. Walk 10–15 minutes into the old town and Little Venice — no transfers needed.
b11: Best times: December for the famous Christmas markets; spring and early summer for the flowers along the canals.
b12: Go early or stay over — day-trippers fill the old town midday; mornings and evenings are magical and quiet.
b13: Pair it with Strasbourg or the Alsace wine route, all easy by train.
b14: You've seen it. Now go. There's a direct TGV from Paris — book your seat and you're a short walk from Little Venice. Every operator, one secure checkout.

b22: The secret no one tells you: you don't need a car or a connection. There's a direct TGV from Paris to Colmar in about 2h20, and Colmar station is a flat 10–15 minute walk from the old town and Little Venice. Step off the train and you're almost there.
